'''Michael Newton Barber''' (born 30 April 1947) is a [[mathematician]], [[physicist]] and academic. He was Vice-Chancellor of [[Flinders University]] in [[South Australia]] from 2008 until 2014.

== Career ==
Barber studied at the [[University of New South Wales]], where he received the University Medal in applied mathematics and graduated with first class honours. He received a PhD from [[Cornell University]] in the USA in theoretical physics in 1972.
He is best known for the scaling theory of finite size effects at [[phase transition]]s, which he introduced together with [[Michael Fisher]].

Barber worked at the [[Australian National University]] and [[University of New South Wales]] as an academic in the 1970s and 1980s. in 1990, he was appointed Dean of the Faculty of Science at the ANU.

He assumed his first office-bearing position as pro vice-chancellor (research) at the [[University of Western Australia]] in 1994 and held the position until 2002. That year, Barber was appointed executive director of science planning at the [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation|CSIRO]]. In 2006, he was appointed group executive of information, manufacturing and minerals. He held this position until his appointment as vice-chancellor at Flinders University in 2008—a position he held until December 2014. During his time as vice-chancellor he worked "to enhance the University’s contribution to the ‘new South Australia’ with its strong defence and resources sectors."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.flinders.edu.au/about/governance/university-officers/vice-chancellor.cfm |title=Vice-Chancellor - Flinders University |date=2013-08-01 |access-date=2016-04-18 |url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130801201223/http://www.flinders.edu.au/about/governance/university-officers/vice-chancellor.cfm |archivedate=1 August 2013 }}</ref> In 2008 he stated: "The University is already more engaged with the defence and resource industries than many people recognise but we need to further strengthen the science and technology base at Flinders so that the University is better positioned to grasp more of the opportunities in the new South Australia. We need to work through this in a planned and deliberate way to find appropriate strategies to address it."<ref>{{Cite web|url= http://blogs.flinders.edu.au/flinders-news/2008/01/02/enhancing-flinders-role-in-the-economy/|title= Flinders News - Blog Archive - Enhancing Flinders' role in the economy|website= blogs.flinders.edu.au|access-date= 2016-04-18|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20121114153508/http://blogs.flinders.edu.au/flinders-news/2008/01/02/enhancing-flinders-role-in-the-economy/|archive-date= 14 November 2012|url-status= dead}}</ref>

In 2012, Barber was a member of the South Australian State Advisory Council of the [[Committee for Economic Development of Australia]] (CEDA).<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://www.ceda.com.au/about/governance/state-advisory-councils/south-australia |title=South Australian state advisory council |date=2012-03-21 |access-date=2016-04-26 |url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120321173447/http://www.ceda.com.au/about/governance/state-advisory-councils/south-australia |archivedate= 21 March 2012 }}</ref>

That same year, Barber's salary for his position as vice-chancellor of Flinders University became a controversial topic. ''[[The Advertiser (Adelaide)|The Advertiser]]'' revealed that he would receive between $710,000 and $719,999 in 2012. In 2010 his salary had been $545,000. A spokesperson from Flinders University stated that his remuneration was "in line" with industry standards.<ref>{{Cite news |url= http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/boost-in-annual-pay-for-flinders-university-vice-chancellor-professor-michael-barber/story-e6frg6n6-1226409620301 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130818165036/http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/boost-in-annual-pay-for-flinders-university-vice-chancellor-professor-michael-barber/story-e6frg6n6-1226409620301 |url-status= dead |archive-date= 18 August 2013 |title= $160,000 boost in annual pay for Flinders University vice-chancellor Professor Michael Barber |last=Stokes |first=Katrina |date=2012-06-26 |work= |newspaper=The Advertiser |access-date=2016-04-18 |via=}}</ref>

Throughout his career, Barber has acted as an advisor on science and research matters to government and industry in Australia and overseas.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |url= http://www.industry.gov.au/research/ResearchWorkforceIssues/Pages/ResearchWorkforceStrategicAdvisoryGroup.aspx |title= Research Workforce Strategic Advisory Group |website= www.industry.gov.au |language= en |access-date= 2016-04-18 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160425230736/http://www.industry.gov.au/research/ResearchWorkforceIssues/Pages/ResearchWorkforceStrategicAdvisoryGroup.aspx |archive-date= 25 April 2016 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Barber was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in 1992. He served as the organisation's Secretary, Science Policy from 2001 until 2005.<ref name=":0" /> In 2001 he was awarded the [[Centenary Medal]] "for service to Australian society through university administration and scientific research".<ref>[https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1127407  Centenary Medal], 1 January 2001, It's an Honour</ref> In 2009 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).<ref>[http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2009 Class of 2009], SIAM Fellows, fellows.siam.org</ref>

In 2018 Barber was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] (AO) for "distinguished service to higher education administration, and in the field of mathematical physics, particularly statistical mechanics, as an academic and researcher, and through contributions to science policy reform".<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.smh.com.au/national/australia-day-honours-2018-the-full-list-20180125-h0o20j.html |title= Australia Day Honours 2018: The full list |date=2018-01-26 |work= The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date= 2018-01-25 |language=en-AUS}}</ref>
